result: Tachyplesin-NBD accumulation in stationary phase E. coli displays a bimodal distribution at concentrations ≥16 μg mL⁻¹, with low accumulators (median ~2400 a.u.) and high accumulators (median ~28,000 a.u.). This bimodal pattern is conserved across nine E. coli clinical isolates and P. aeruginosa, but not in K. pneumoniae or S. aureus, and is specific to tachyplesin among tested AMPs.

result: Low accumulators retain tachyplesin-NBD primarily on bacterial membranes, while high accumulators accumulate the peptide intracellularly. result: Low accumulators maintain membrane integrity and survive tachyplesin treatment at rates comparable to untreated cells, while high accumulators show significantly reduced survival (p<0.0001). The proportion of low accumulators strongly correlates with population survival (r²=0.98, p<0.0001).

result: Transcriptomic analysis of sorted low and high accumulators revealed 1,563 differentially expressed genes organized into five clusters.
